clue.text: Battle gun knocked Sid about-dished him

definitions.note: made a dish of him: the clue's past participle points at the noun, a mixed dish of chopped meat, eggs and anchovies

indicators.note: knocked signals that the letters which follow are being battered into a new order
about signals that the letters of gun and Sid are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: the Alma was a battle of the Crimean War, fought in 1854

explanation.surface: A gunner in a battle sends poor Sid flying and finishes him off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked' and 'about' together signal the anagram of ALMA (the Crimean battle) with GUN and SID; 'dished him' plays on dished meaning ruined and dished meaning served up as a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a cold mixed dish of chopped meats and pickles, so to be made into it is to be dished up.

clue.text: Guardian of city at that time surrounded by flak

indicators.note: surrounded by means the time word is placed inside the flak letters

parts.note: flak is anti-aircraft fire, abbreviated AA
at that time means then

explanation.surface: A city's protector caught in anti-aircraft fire during an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian of city' looks like a watchman; the goddess was the patron of Athens, the city named for her, and 'surrounded by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom was the patron deity and protector of Athens.

clue.text: Affirm to keep up

definitions.meaning: to affirm is to assert something as true
to keep up is to preserve or continue something

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both: to assert a claim, and to keep a thing going or in repair.

clue.text: Make good repast out of a snail ?

indicators.note: out of signals that the answer is made from the letters of good repast rearranged

explanation.surface: Turn a snail into a fine meal, as the French do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make ... out of' reads as cooking, but 'out of' signals rearranging GOOD REPAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail belongs to the class of molluscs that crawl on a muscular belly-foot, the older spelling of gastropod.

clue.text: The lad has intelligence

indicators.note: has signals that the lad goes with the intelligence beside him, the news word coming first

parts.note: intelligence in the sense of information is news
a lad is a boy

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a boy who carries news: 'intelligence' means information, not brains.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper boy who sells or delivers papers literally carries the latest information.

clue.text: One pro Welshman

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh masculine first name, the Welsh form of Ivor.

clue.text: Hasn't he yet learned to swim ?

definitions.text: Hasn't he yet learned to swim ?

parts.words: Hasn't he yet learned to swim ?
parts.note: a creature thrashing about in water looks like a poor swimmer, but this one is a flatfish, born to swim

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flatfish and a struggling, clumsy movement as in water.

clue.text: Sabrina, your robe is slipping as you rise

definitions.text: Sabrina, your robe is slipping as you rise

parts.note: Sabrina is the nymph or goddess of the River Severn, in Milton's Comus

indicators.note: is slipping signals that the letters of robe slide out of their order

explanation.surface: A nymph rises from the water and her robe slips.
explanation.walkthrough: Sabrina is the Severn's goddess, and 'is slipping' rearranges ROBE; the whole clue pictures the tidal wave that rises up the Severn estuary in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal bore is a wave surging up a river; the Severn's is the best known in Britain.

clue.text: Not always pronouncedly the man of the section to wheel

indicators.note: the word is sometimes, though not always, said the same as the word for a chap; it is also said to rhyme with belly

parts.note: the man, a chap, is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in charge of one section of a wheelworks.
explanation.walkthrough: The rim piece is said either like 'fellow' or like 'felly', so 'Not always' hedges the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the curved pieces making up the rim of a spoked wooden wheel.

clue.text: Cutting links

parts.note: links read as the joined loops of a chain, here doing the cutting rather than being cut

explanation.definitionFit: A power saw whose teeth are mounted on an endless loop of linked segments.

clue.text: Father to charge for the port say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so the pair sounds like the place

parts.note: father is sire and to charge is to accuse

explanation.surface: A father bringing an accusation about the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the sound-alike: SIRE + ACCUSE spoken sounds like the Sicilian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Syracuse is an ancient seaport on the east coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Airborne troops in Brazil ?

definitions.meaning: a northern state of Brazil, with Belem as its capital, bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: A short form for parachute soldiers, and the name of a state on the Amazon delta.

clue.text: Such was Hudson's diurnal idleness

parts.note: W. H. Hudson wrote the book Idle Days in the South American land at the tip of the continent

explanation.walkthrough: 'diurnal idleness' unpacks to 'idle days', from the title of Hudson's 1893 book.
explanation.definitionFit: Hudson's idle days were spent in the far south of Argentina, so they belonged to that region.

clue.text: Higher than Tennyson's high hall one

definitions.text: Higher than Tennyson's high hall one

parts.words: Higher than Tennyson's high hall one
parts.note: Tennyson's Maud has birds in the high Hall-garden; a plot even higher would sit on top of the building

explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for garden, completing Tennyson's phrase 'high Hall-garden' from Maud.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted terrace laid out on the top of a building, higher than any hall's grounds.

clue.text: Results of calligraphic errors or spirit communications ?

definitions.meaning: words that got into dictionaries only through copying or printing mistakes
messages that might come from phantoms at a seance

explanation.definitionFit: Lexicographers' term for words that never truly existed, read literally as utterances of a spectre.

clue.text: Townshend had a name for them

definitions.text: Townshend had a name for them

parts.words: Townshend had a name for them
parts.note: the eighteenth-century politician Viscount Townshend championed a root crop so keenly he earned it as his nickname

explanation.walkthrough: Charles, 2nd Viscount Townshend, was known as 'Turnip' Townshend for promoting the root vegetable in English crop rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Townshend's nickname came from these root vegetables, which he grew as winter fodder.

clue.text: Cecilia ?

parts.note: the girl's name read as Cecil plus the place-name ending -ia: a land named after Cecil, the empire-builder

explanation.walkthrough: The colony was named after Cecil Rhodes, so a land called after Cecil might be 'Cecil-ia'.
explanation.definitionFit: The former African territory, now Zambia and Zimbabwe, took its name from the colonialist Cecil Rhodes.

clue.text: See what's on your number plate in a Swiss resort?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a number plate shows the car number

explanation.surface: Check your registration plate while holidaying in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is the archaic 'behold'; CAR NO is the car number shown on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Locarno is a lakeside town in Ticino, the Italian-speaking south of Switzerland.

clue.text: Cupid in Italy

parts.note: the Italian word for a little love god, the winged boy of paintings

explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian name for a putto or small figure of the god of love.

clue.text: Reveals thus some always in salt

indicators.note: in means the always word goes inside the salt word

parts.note: sal is the chemist's Latin for salt, as in sal volatile
ever means always

explanation.surface: Revealing some secrets is always a pinch of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reveals thus' offers a second route: the letters of 'Reveals' rearranged spell the same word, so the clue has two wordplays leading to one answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a number more than two but not many, as in a few items.

clue.text: Annual charge as result of earthquake

definitions.meaning: a yearly payment made by a leaseholder to the freeholder for the land
earth that has been torn apart, ground that is split

explanation.definitionFit: A leaseholder's yearly fee for land, and read literally, earth that has been torn open.

clue.text: Return concerning Hyde rather than Jekyll

parts.note: to return is to go back, so the word go turned back
concerning means re, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A report about the two sides of Stevenson's split character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' gives OG: go, written back. Mr Hyde is the monstrous side of Dr Jekyll.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde is the brute half of the pair, a monster like a fairy-tale giant who eats people.

clue.text: Be very respectful of the parson going before

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman, abbreviated Rev for Reverend
ere means before

explanation.surface: Show great respect for the vicar walking in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour deeply is to hold someone in awe and esteem.

clue.text: Cold ?No matches. So what ?

parts.note: without matches, the cold sufferer must make flame the ancient way, by rubbing wood together

explanation.definitionFit: A fire kindled by friction of wood, used in folk ritual against cattle disease, made when flame was wanted.

clue.text: In a way it's short this month

parts.note: taken as written
a way or road is a street, ST

explanation.surface: Somehow the month seems shorter this year.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an abbreviation: the letter-writer's short form of 'instant', meaning of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: Old business letters used this short form of instant to mean of the current month.

clue.text: Bits 'of Welsh rabbit for instance ?

parts.note: Welsh rabbit is also called Welsh rarebit, so its bits are rare bits, things seldom found

explanation.definitionFit: Things seldom found, which run together as 'rare bits' sound like the cheese dish.

clue.text: Ici on parle Fran ais in Arden

definitions.meaning: French is spoken here, as in a French cathedral city on the Somme
a lord attending the exiled duke in Arden in As You Like It

explanation.definitionFit: A French city in Picardy, and a courtier in Shakespeare's forest comedy.

clue.text: Enchanting viewers ?

parts.note: the saying is that distance lends enchantment to the view; instruments that magnify distant objects lend it to viewers

explanation.definitionFit: Optical instruments that make distant objects appear near, for astronomers and sightseers.
